To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

vitamin E and monensin supplementation did not minimise the trans-10 isomer formation in the rumen of dairy cows fed with whole cottonseed and had no beneficial effects on milk yield and milk fat content of dairy cows.
supplementing lactating dairy cows' diets containing whole cottonseed with monensin or/and vitamin E did not minimise the milk fat depression and did not affect the milk fat profile.
vitamin E and monensin supplement in the diets of dairy cows containing whole-cottonseed did not improve milk production and composition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of monensin, vitamin E, and their combination, in diets containing whole cottonseed on milk yield, milk composition and milk FA profile.

the effects of monesin and vitamin E supplementation to the diets of lactation dairy cows containing whole cotonsed, as the main sources of fatty acids on the efficiency of N utilisation and efficiency of NEL utilisation.
the effects of monesin and vitamin E supplementations on milk production and milk fatty acid composition of lactating Holstein dairy cows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inclusion of whole cottonseed as a main source of FA in the diet did not cause milk fat depression and supplementing vitamin E and/or ionophore did not improve milk yield or composition.
the inclusion of whole cottonseed in the diet of lactating dairy cow at the level of 570 g/kg DM in the concentrate mixture, as used in this study, did not impair milk fat synthesis.

the dietary supplementation of vitamin E and/or Monensin did not improve milk production, composition, efficiency of utilising N and NE, and nutrients digestibilities in lactating dairy cows fed with a diet containing whole cottonseed as the main source for fatty acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vitamin E and monensin did not have an effect on feed intake and milk production and composition.
the inclusion of whole cottonseed in the diet of lactating dairy cow is not an efficient strategy to reduce the milk fat content and to minimise the formation of the trans-10 FA in the rumen.

vitamin E and monensin supplement in the diet of lactating dairy cow fed with cottonseed did not have any effect on the efficiency of nitrogen utilisation, efficiency NE utilisation, milk yield, milk composition and milk fatty acid profile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
feeding whole cottonseed as the main source for FA did not depress milk production and composition and did not increase the concentration of trans-10 CLA in the milk fat.
vitamin E and monensin do not improve milk fat concentration in lactating dairy cows when whole cottonseed is included in the diet.
vitamin E and monensin do not prevent the milk fat depression caused by the inclusion of whole cottonseed in the ration of lactating dairy cow.
